contests.name: All Asian DX Contest, CW
contests.exchange: RS(T) and the operator's age. An operator who does not want to send an age sends 01. Multi-operator stations send the average age of the operators at the start of the contest.
contests.source_note: jarl.org (67th All Asian DX Contest rule): 'CW: (June 20-21,2026) From 00:00 UTC on the third Saturday in June to 24:00 UTC on the following day'. Bands: 'Amateur bands 160m, 80m, 40m, 20m, 15m, 10m'. Power: 'Low Power: Total output power must not exceed 100 watts. High Power: There is no limitation on total output power within the maximum allowable power level established by the national licensing authority'. The third Saturday in June 2026 is June 20, which is the date JARL prints. LOG DEADLINE DELIBERATELY NOT ENCODED: JARL states 'Logs must arrive at JARL no later than 10 days after the event is over. CW...July 1, 2026'. July 1 is 10 days after the last contest DAY (June 21), not 10 days after the 24:00 UTC end instant this record stores, so log_deadline_days would have to be 9 to reproduce JARL's own date. Rather than print a number JARL never wrote, the rule is quoted here and the field is omitted. Logs also go to aacw@jarl.org.
contests.summary: JARL's CW leg of the All Asian DX Contest: 24 hours over the third weekend in June, exchanging signal report and the operator's age.

eligibility.note: Anyone may enter. Asian stations work everyone; non-Asian stations score only contacts with Asian stations -- JARL: 'The points of completed contacts with Asian stations ... are shown below.' contests.name: Jock White Memorial Field Day
contests.exchange: RS(T), a serial number starting at 001, and an NZART branch number (home stations use 00)
contests.note: NZART SETS THIS ONE BY THE NEW ZEALAND CLOCK, NOT BY UTC: 1500-2400 Saturday and 0600-1500 Sunday NZDT. The UTC instants shown here therefore move with New Zealand daylight saving, unlike almost every other contest in this calendar. The QRP category is '5 Watts CW/10 Watts SSB maximum'; the 100W figure is NZART's overall limit. The log deadline is 'the Saturday which is four weeks after the Field Day Saturday' -- anchored to the Saturday rather than to either session's end -- so no interval is computed.
contests.source_note: nzart.org.nz (Jock White Memorial Field Day rules): 'The last full weekend in February each year: on Saturday 1500-2400 NZDT and Sunday 0600-1500 NZDT. NOTE: when February only has three full weekends then field day will be held on Saturday 28th February and Sunday 1st March. This is to avoid a clash with the ARRL International CW contest. This will occur in 2026.' The exclusion is encoded exactly, not approximated: the last-full-weekend Saturday falls on February 21 if and only if February has 28 days and February 1 is a Sunday -- which is precisely the three-full-weekend case -- so exclude_dates [[2, 21]] pushes it to February 28 and reproduces NZART's own 2026 dates. 'Last Saturday in February' was tested and rejected: it diverges in a leap year beginning on a Saturday. Bands, modes and power: '40 and/or 80 metres, PHONE (SSB) and/or CW, 100 watts PEP maximum.' Exchange and log deadline as quoted in note.
contests.summary: NZART's branch field day: two evening-and-morning sessions on the last full weekend in February, 80 and 40 metres, run on New Zealand time.

eligibility.note: There is an entry category for 'Overseas stations in the Oceania Region', and contacts may be made 'with any other field, ZL home or overseas (Oceania) station'. In practice this is a New Zealand event with an Oceania fringe.

contests.name: NZART Sangster Shield
contests.exchange: New Zealand stations send RST, a serial number starting at 001 and their branch number; overseas stations send RST and a serial number
contests.note: A low-power contest by design, running since 1927: 'The output of the transmitter must not exceed 5 Watts PEP. Overseas contestants may use any power up to the maximum permitted by their license.' Three hours, worked as six half-hour periods. NZART moved to this one-night format for 2026.
contests.source_note: nzart.org.nz (NZART Sangster Shield rules): 'Third Saturday of May each year, between the hours of 0800-1100 UTC (2000 NZST-2300 NZST) on Saturday evening. The maximum period of operation will be three hours (6 operating periods of 30 minutes each).' Times are stated in UTC, so unlike the Jock White Field Day this record is not wall-clock. Band: '80m'. Power as quoted in note. Exchange as quoted. Log deadline: 'on or before the fourth Saturday after the contest', which is exactly the stored end instant plus 28 days, so the interval is encoded; logs go to sangster@nzart.org.nz. Checked against the date NZART prints on the same page: 'The next Sangster Shield contest will be held on Saturday 16th May 2026', and the third Saturday of May 2026 is May 16.
contests.summary: NZART's oldest contest, a three-hour 5-watt CW event on 80 metres on the third Saturday evening in May.

eligibility.note: NZART: contacts count 'CW to CW between New Zealand stations and between New Zealand and overseas stations only' -- an overseas entrant can only work ZL.

contests.name: NZART Memorial Contest
contests.bands_note: Suggested frequencies CW 3520-3550 kHz, SSB 3610-3660 kHz
contests.exchange: RS(T) and a three-digit serial number starting at 001
contests.note: Held every year since 1946 for the New Zealand amateurs who died in the Second World War. Three one-hour periods; a station may be worked once per period on each of SSB and CW. The QRP category is '5W CW/10W SSB maximum'. The log deadline is a fixed date, 'Logs must arrive no later than 31 July', not an interval, so none is computed; logs go to contests@nzart.org.nz.
contests.source_note: nzart.org.nz (NZART Memorial Contest rules): 'First Saturday in July each year 0800 - 1100 UTC (2000 - 2300 NZST) Three one-hour operating periods.' Band: '80m only - A station may be contacted twice during each operating period - once on SSB and once on CW'. Mode categories: 'Mixed mode - SSB and CW', 'CW only', 'SSB only'. Power: 'Open - 100W maximum CW/SSB' and 'QRP - 5W CW/10W SSB maximum'. Exchange as quoted. Checked against the date NZART prints on the same page: 'The next Memorial Contest date is Saturday 4th July 2026', and the first Saturday in July 2026 is July 4.
contests.summary: NZART's memorial contest for amateurs lost in the Second World War: three hours on 80 metres on the first Saturday evening in July.

eligibility.note: Multipliers are ZL, VK and Oceania prefixes, so the scoring is built around New Zealand and its neighbours.

contests.name: ZL Autumn and Winter Sprints, CW
contests.bands_note: Suggested frequencies CW 3520-3550 kHz
contests.exchange: RS(T) and the outside temperature to the nearest degree; on CW, 'm' denotes a minus sign
contests.note: One of three back-to-back 29-minute sprints on the same evening, each in a different mode and each scored separately, which is why they are three records here rather than one. Logs are due 'within 24 hours of the end of the sprint' -- shorter than a day, so no deadline interval is computed; they go to markzl3ab@gmail.com.
contests.source_note: nzart.org.nz (ZL Autumn and Winter Sprints rules): 'Each Tuesday in April and August: 0800-0829 UTC (2000-2029 NZST) CW only / 0830-0859 UTC (2030-2059 NZST) SSB only / 0900-0929 UTC (2100-2129 NZST) FT4 only'. Band: '80m'. Categories: 'Single Operator, one transmitted signal only, use of the DX cluster is allowed and one of: 100w maximum (by convention Low Power in your contest logger); or QRP - up to 5W CW, 10W SSB and 5W FT4'. Exchange: 'CW/SSB RS(T) report and Outside Temperature to the nearest degree.' Scoring: 'Each mode will be scored separately.'
contests.summary: A 29-minute CW sprint on 80 metres every Tuesday evening in April and August, exchanging a report and the outside temperature.

eligibility.note: NZART states no geographic restriction, but it is a New Zealand 80-metre evening sprint and the practical range says so.

contests.name: LABRE DX Contest
contests.bands_note: Only the 1.8, 3.5, 7, 14, 21, and 28 MHz bands may be used
contests.exchange: Brazilian stations send RS(T) and their two-letter state abbreviation; stations outside Brazil send RS(T) and a two-letter continent code
contests.note: LABRE prints a log submission link, https://www.labre.org.br/sendlog, which returned 404 when this record was checked; entries can also be raised with contest@labre.org.br. No log_submit_url is recorded rather than one that does not resolve.
contests.source_note: LABRE DX Contest 2026 rules (https://www.labre.org.br/contest/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Regulamento-Contest-LABRE-DX-2026-Ingles-v3.pdf, linked from the contest page): 'Date: 3rd (third) weekend of July. Start: 00:00 UTC on Saturday, July 18th. End: 23:59 UTC on Sunday, July 19st.' Objective: 'For amateurs worldwide to contact as many amateurs from Brazil'. Bands as quoted in bands_note; modes SSB, CW and MIXED; power High up to 1500 W, Low up to 100 W, QRP up to 5 W. Log deadline: 'XIII. LOG DEADLINE: All entries must send their logs WITHIN FIVE (5) DAYS after the end of the contest.' The third full weekend of July 2026 is July 18-19, which is what LABRE prints. rules_url is the contest hub rather than the PDF, whose path embeds the month it was uploaded.
contests.summary: Brazil's international contest: 48 hours over the third weekend in July, with Brazilian stations sending their state.

eligibility.note: LABRE: 'For amateurs worldwide to contact as many amateurs from Brazil' -- everyone enters, and Brazil is the target.

contests.name: North Jakarta ORARI DX Contest
contests.bands_note: Contact should made on 3.5, 7, 14, 21 and 28 MHz. No WARC bands.
contests.exchange: Indonesian stations send 5/9 and ORARI; stations outside Indonesia send 5/9 and DX
contests.note: Run by ORARI Lokal Jakarta Utara to mark ORARI's anniversary. There is one entry category, 'Single Operator All Band Any Power', with 'Power maximal depend on the regulations in each Country', so no power ladder is recorded.
contests.source_note: oraricontest.id (Rules for outside Indonesia -- North Jakarta ORARI DX CONTEST): 'Time: Every June 2nd Weekend', 'Contest will start: 13 June 2026 -> 00:00 UTC - 23:59 UTC ( 24 Hours )'. Bands: 'Contact should made on 3.5, 7, 14, 21 and 28 MHz. No WARC bands.' Exchange: 'All Indonesia Stations : 5/9 + ORARI' and 'DX Stations outside Indonesia : 5/9 DX'. Log deadline: 'All logs must be sent within 7 (seven) days after the end of contest'. The rule is checked against all four dates ORARI publishes on the same page -- June 13 2026, June 12 2027, June 10 2028 and June 9 2029 -- and the second full weekend of June matches every one.
contests.summary: Indonesia's anniversary DX contest: 24 hours of SSB on the second June weekend, with YB stations as the multiplier everyone wants.

eligibility.note: ORARI: 'For amateurs around the world to contact as many other amateurs in as many countries and Indonesia ( YB Land ) stations. Everyone Worked Everyone'.
